why_winner: C is the only draft whose first three lines carry all three of the confession, the hero ratio, and the admission that the reader is trusting a chart that hides 98% of the number, which is the exact contrarian property the tracker scores highest (naming something the audience does but will not admit). A takes four lines to reach the ratio, and B opens in second person, which turns the same insight into a lecture and gives away the mistake as somebody else's.

runner_up_notes.A: The list-rate cost anchor, phrased as 'what that same work prices at' rather than a bill. C drops the magnitude entirely, so 213 to 1 floats without scale.
runner_up_notes.B: 'Two levers moved the number, and neither was a better prompt.' That clause pre-empts the reader's assumption that this is a prompting problem, and C's transition does not.

issues.description: C states the mechanism (cost is average context times number of calls, growing with the square of turn count) but never shows it. The single most vivid fact in the source, that one 21k-token file read at call 200 of a 947-call session gets re-read 747 more times for roughly 15M tokens, is absent. It is also the only fact in the post the reader can act on within the next hour.
issues.action: Graft in the re-read illustration immediately after the mechanism line, as one short beat. Cut the 5.4-hour session detail to pay for it, since the 947-call figure survives inside the new line.

issues.description: The plan's structure calls for the scale of the number, and C carries no cost anchor at all. 213 to 1 is a ratio without a magnitude, so a reader can read it as a curiosity rather than a problem.
issues.action: Borrow A's framing: one line pricing the week at published list rates, explicitly labelled an equivalence and not an invoice.

issues.description: Line 5, 'The legend was a slice', is past tense and reads as though the chart has since been fixed. It has not. The reader's chart is doing this right now.
issues.action: Move to present tense so it indicts the reader's own dashboard, not just Altaf's past one.
